about.syntaxText: The command line of the routers and switches is modelled on the syntax of FRRouting (vtysh). It is an independent, simplified reproduction for teaching and contains no code or text from FRRouting. FRRouting is a separate project under the GPL-2.0 license and is not affiliated with this simulator.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: The Network Simulator does not process personal data: no accounts, no names, no e-mail addresses, no tracking, no advertising, no external services.
privacy.local: Projects stay on this device (in the browser storage or as a file you save yourself). Nothing is transmitted; the page technically cannot connect to the Internet.
privacy.sessions: Sessions only contain the network configuration (devices, cables, settings) under a random code. They are deleted automatically {hours} hours after the last change, or immediately with “Delete session”.
privacy.classes: Class sessions only carry a class label without personal reference (e.g. “INF22a”). Teachers see codes and results, but no names.
privacy.feedback: Feedback only contains the entered text, the program version and the language; it is deleted after {days} days.
privacy.noIp: IP addresses are neither stored nor logged. To prevent abuse, the server briefly counts requests in memory, anonymised.
privacy.storage: Only technically necessary values are stored in the browser (session code, language, appearance). There are no cookies.
privacy.rules: The concept follows the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (revFADP) and the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR): data minimisation, purpose limitation, short retention and privacy by design. Please do not enter names or other personal data in feedback or labels.
privacy.rights: The school or person operating a web version is the controller. Sessions can be deleted by yourself at any time; the operator deletes everything else on request or automatically when the period expires.

catalog.twoPcs.title: Connect two computers
catalog.twoPcs.description: Connect PC 1 and PC 2 directly with a cable and give both an IP address in the same network, e.g. 192.168.1.1/24 and 192.168.1.2/24. Test with ping in action mode.
catalog.twoPcs.goal2: Both are in the same network.
catalog.twoPcs.hint2: Same subnet mask and same network part of the address.
catalog.switchLan.title: Small LAN with a switch
catalog.switchLan.description: Connect all three devices to the switch and give them addresses in the same network.
catalog.switchLan.goal1: PC 1 is connected to the switch.
catalog.switchLan.goal2: The notebook is connected to the switch.
catalog.switchLan.goal3: All three are in the same network.
catalog.switchLan.goal4: The notebook reaches PC 1 by ping.
catalog.twoSubnets.title: Two networks with a router
catalog.twoSubnets.description: PC 1 and PC 2 should be in different networks and reach each other via the router. The router needs an address in each network; the PCs enter it as their default gateway.
catalog.twoSubnets.goal1: PC 1 and PC 2 are in different networks.
catalog.twoSubnets.hint4: Gateway = address of the router in the own network.
catalog.dhcp.title: Assign addresses via DHCP
catalog.dhcp.description: The server should assign addresses to the three notebooks as DHCP server. Set up the service and switch the notebooks to DHCP.
catalog.dhcp.goal1: Notebook 1 receives an address via DHCP.
catalog.dhcp.goal2: Notebook 2 receives an address via DHCP.
catalog.dhcp.goal3: Notebook 3 receives an address via DHCP.
catalog.dhcp.goal4: Notebook 3 reaches the server by ping.
catalog.dhcp.hint1: The address range must be in the server's network.
catalog.webDns.title: Open a web page via DNS
catalog.webDns.description: The web server serves a page. Set up the name www.schule.ch on the DNS server and enter the DNS server on the notebook so that the page can be reached by name.
catalog.webDns.goal1: The notebook reaches the web server by ping.
catalog.webDns.goal2: The page loads via the IP address.
catalog.webDns.goal3: The page loads via the name www.schule.ch.
catalog.webDns.hint3: A record www.schule.ch → 10.1.1.80; DNS server on the notebook: 10.1.1.53.
catalog.wlan.title: WLAN in the classroom
catalog.wlan.description: Set up a wireless network with a password on the access point, give the notebooks the WLAN profile and an address, and connect them wirelessly (connection type “Wireless”).
catalog.wlan.goal1: Notebook 1 reaches the server by ping.
catalog.wlan.hint1: SSID and password must be the same on the access point and notebook; the LED on the wireless link must be green.
catalog.vlans.title: Separate networks with VLANs
catalog.vlans.description: All four PCs are in the same IP network. Separate administration and teaching on the switch with two VLANs, without changing the addresses.
catalog.vlans.hint3: Administration access ports in VLAN 10, teaching in VLAN 20 (Pro mode).
catalog.roas.title: Router-on-a-stick
catalog.roas.description: The PCs are in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20. Connect the router to the switch with a single cable and route between the VLANs via subinterfaces with an 802.1Q tag.
catalog.roas.goal1: The router is connected to the switch.
catalog.roas.goal2: There is at most one router.
catalog.roas.hint3: Switch: PC ports as access ports in VLAN 10/20, router port as trunk. Router: eth0.10 and eth0.20.
catalog.l3.title: Campus with layer 3 switch and fiber
catalog.l3.description: Connect the core switch to both buildings via fiber (SFP modules!). Each building gets its own VLAN and network; the core routes between them and relays DHCP requests to the central server.
catalog.l3.goal2: The core is connected to building A.
catalog.l3.goal3: The core is connected to building B.
catalog.l3.goal4: Notebook A receives an address via DHCP.
catalog.l3.goal5: Notebook B receives an address via DHCP.
catalog.l3.goal6: Notebook A reaches the DHCP server.
catalog.l3.hint2: Same SFP modules on both sides, connection type “Fiber”, uplinks as trunk.
catalog.l3.hint4: SVIs vlan10/vlan20 with ip helper-address 10.99.0.10; on the server one scope per network.
